english.title: Direct supplier of small quantities of meat fail keep, retain and make available records

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: food safety and hygiene England regulations 2013

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a producer who supplied meat in the manner described in paragraph 1 of Schedule 5 to the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013, failed to

(A)_[keep a record in adequate form to show the number of birds and the number of lagomorphs received into, and the amount of fresh meat despatched from your premises during each week]_
(B)_[retain the record required under paragraph 2(2)(a) of Schedule 5 to the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013 for a period of one year]_
(C)_[make the record required under paragraph 2(2)(a) of Schedule 5 to the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013 available to an authorised officer, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFICER..), on request]_
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraphs 2(2) and 3 of Schedule 5 to, and regulation 19(2) of, the Food Safety and Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
small scale meat producer and supplier
fail to keep adequate records, retain them for a year and make them available to authorised officer on request

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
